findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so the shown cache status goes stale
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. It never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The disconnect mutation a few lines below does invalidate that query. Since cacheUpdatedAt comes from connectedCalendars, after a successful delete the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Last updated' timestamp and keeps offering 'Delete cached data' unless the parent's onChanged happens to refetch. The PR's test plan explicitly checks that the UI updates after deletion. Invalidate the query in onSuccess or onSettled, as the disconnect path does.

findings.title: Backfilling updatedAt with NOW() makes every legacy cache row report the deploy time as its last update
findings.body: The column is added with DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets updatedAt equal to the migration execution time. The new UI shows 'Last updated: <timestamp>' from this value, so all pre-existing caches will show a fabricated recent timestamp until they are rewritten. There is no real value to backfill from, but the UI should either treat legacy rows as unknown (nullable column or a separate display rule) or the PR should document that the timestamp is not meaningful for them.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the SQL that follows it
findings.body: The header says the required updatedAt column was added 'without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' The statement below does add a default (DEFAULT NOW()) precisely so it works on a non-empty table. The comment is misleading for anyone reading the migration history and should be corrected or removed.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US instead of the user's locale
findings.body: Intl.DateTimeFormat is constructed with the fixed locale 'en-US', while the surrounding text is translated through useLocale. Users with other UI languages will see the timestamp in US format next to a localized label. Use the locale from useLocale (or the i18n language) when formatting the date.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, which is unrelated to this feature and relies on an undeclared, unpinned dependency
findings.body: tsx is not listed in apps/web devDependencies (ts-node still is), so 'npx tsx' downloads whatever version the registry serves at run time. That adds network dependence and a non-reproducible toolchain to the dev:cron script. The change has nothing to do with calendar cache management, so it should be separated, or tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency and the behaviour of cron-tester.ts under tsx verified.

findings.title: Every cache refresh now issues an unconditional UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential
findings.body: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) runs on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache call. It touches every selected calendar for the credential, across all event types, to bump updatedAt. The PR notes say nothing in the frontend reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this is extra write load on a hot path with no consumer. Either drop it or justify the consumer in code.

findings.title: Unused columns added to the session user query and to UserWithCalendars
findings.body: updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select in findUnlockedUserForSession, which runs on session lookups. Nothing in this diff reads them. The same fields were also made required in the UserWithCalendars type in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts, so every caller building that type must now supply them, which is an unnecessary type-level break. Remove them unless a concrete consumer is added in this PR.

findings.title: The only authorization guard for cache deletion has no test
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler is the sole check preventing a user from deleting another user's calendar cache: it looks up the credential by id and userId before deleting. No test accompanies the change, and the same is true for getCacheStatusByCredentialIds and the new enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler. A test for the not-owned and not-found cases is needed before merging.

findings.title: Access-denied case throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body: When the credential is missing or belongs to another user, the handler throws a generic Error. Through tRPC this becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so the client cannot distinguish a bad id from a server fault. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code.

findings.title: Actions column is always rendered, leaving blank space for delegated or locked credentials
findings.body: Previously the actions prop was a falsy expression for delegated credentials or when connection modification was disabled, so no actions container was rendered. Now a flex w-32 div is always passed, and CredentialActionsDropdown returns null in those cases. Each card reserves an empty 8rem column where the old UI showed nothing. Pass undefined/false when the dropdown would render nothing, or have the component own its container.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only; on Linux the env update silently fails while the script still reports success
findings.body: GNU sed interprets the empty string after -i as the script and then treats the substitution expression as a filename, so the substitution never happens. The script has no set -e or exit check, so it prints 'Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL' regardless. Use a portable approach (e.g. a temp file and mv) and check the result.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is a relative path resolved against the caller's cwd, not the script location
findings.body: ENV_FILE is set to '../.env'. Run from the repo root this writes to the parent directory of the repository, not the repo's .env. The path should be resolved from the script's own directory (e.g. dirname of $0).

findings.title: Failure paths exit with status 0
findings.body: cleanup() ends with 'exit 0', and it is also the failure path when no tunnel URL could be extracted or the rate limit is hit. Callers and CI cannot detect that the webhook setup failed. Propagate a non-zero exit code on the failure paths.

findings.title: Reusing an externally started tmole takes its URL from an unrelated or stale log file
findings.body: When a tmole process is already running, the script extracts the URL from /tmp/tmole.log. That process may have been started by hand or with different output, so the log may be missing or contain a previous, dead tunnel URL. The stale URL is then written into GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in .env with no check that it is live.
